n: David becomes discouraged and decides, in his own heart rather than by asking the Lord, that he will eventually die by Saul's hand. He plans to flee to Philistine territory where Saul won't follow.

f.g: Notably, there is no mention of David inquiring of the Lord here, unlike in chapter 23.

n: David and his six hundred men go to Achish, king of Gath — the same king before whom David once pretended to be insane. Now he comes as a known rebel against Saul.
David and his men settle in Gath with their families, including David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail.
When Saul hears that David has fled to Gath, he stops pursuing him. David's plan works.
David asks Achish for a town in the countryside, humbly suggesting he isn't worthy to live in the royal city. It also gives him freedom from close watching.
Achish gives David the town of Ziklag. The narrator notes that it has belonged to Judah's kings ever since — written from a later perspective.

f.g: A town in the Negev (southern desert), originally allotted to Judah and Simeon.

n: David lives in Philistine territory for sixteen months.

f.w: a full year and four months
f.g: Literally “days and four months” — possibly a year and four months.

n: From Ziklag David raids the Geshurites, Girzites, and Amalekites — longtime enemies of Israel living in the south toward Egypt.
David leaves no survivors and takes the livestock and goods back to Achish. This is a hard passage; David is a fugitive warlord in a brutal age, and the narrator reports rather than praises it.
When Achish asks where they raided, David lies, naming southern regions of Judah and its allies so Achish thinks he's attacking his own people.

f.g: A clan within Judah in the Negev.

n: David kills everyone so that no witnesses can report what he's really doing. Deception has drawn him into deeper violence.
Achish believes David has made himself hated among Israel, and so will be his loyal servant forever. The deception has worked — but it will put David in a dangerous position soon.

f.g: Literally “become a stench” to his people.
